Which is cheaper in Orlando right now?

Westgate is cheaper at entry, and by a wide margin. Our tracked Orlando inventory shows Westgate packages averaging $201 with a low of $49, versus Wyndham averaging $224 with a low around $199. That $150 gap at the floor is the whole story for budget shoppers: a Westgate teaser weekend can cost less than a single Orlando hotel night, while Wyndham's cheapest tracked offers cluster near two hundred dollars. Price alone is not the deal. Westgate's Orlando anchor is the sprawling Westgate Lakes and Westgate Vacation Villas near the parks, which is where most of its sub-$100 teasers route. Presentation length compared

Plan for about two hours either way. Westgate's event-style Orlando previews run around 120 minutes, and Wyndham's fall in the standard 90-to-120-minute band. Neither brand is meaningfully shorter, so the tiebreaker is price and resort, not time saved. Budget for the full stated window plus the walk to the sales suite and the closer at the end.

Book Westgate if you want the lowest possible Orlando entry price and you are flexible on which resort you sample. Book Wyndham if you specifically want a Wyndham-network property such as Bonnet Creek, or you already hold Wyndham points and want to see the brand before committing further. Both require the same declinable preview, so the deciding factors are the resort you actually want and the dollars at the floor. How we compare these Orlando prices

Every figure on this page comes from prices we scrape directly from live listings, not from brand advertising or slug guesses. We log each price as a dated snapshot, so an average reflects what the brand actually charged over time rather than a one-day teaser. For Westgate, 159 tracked Orlando-area deals give us a dense picture of both the $49 floor and the $201 typical price; for Wyndham, 6 tracked deals mean the sample is smaller and the floor near $199 moves less. That difference in sample size is itself useful information: a brand you can find at a low price on almost any day is more practically cheap than one whose low price is rare.

Beyond price, weigh three practical factors before you choose. First, dates: Westgate's park-corridor resorts and Wyndham's Bonnet Creek both fill fast in peak season, so a low advertised price means little if your week is sold out. Second, party size, because the package price is per unit, a family splitting a $99 Westgate weekend pays far less per head than two people splitting a $224 Wyndham stay. Third, your tolerance for the pitch: both run a declinable presentation near two hours, and the discount is only a true saving if you can comfortably say no. If you weight all three and price still leads, Westgate is the Orlando pick; if a specific Wyndham resort or your existing points tip the scale, the premium is defensible. The verdict: For pure price, Westgate wins Orlando — $49 floor, $201 average, and 159 live deals to Wyndham's 6. Choose Wyndham only when you want a specific network resort and will pay roughly $150 more at the floor to get it.
